method: Each thumbnail samples the centre of an equal slice of the clip, so the sampling interval is duration divided by the number of thumbnails and sample i sits at (i + 0.5) times that interval. A sample's frame number is its timestamp times the frame rate, rounded to the nearest whole frame and clamped to the clip's last frame, where the clip holds the frame rate times duration rounded to whole frames. Thumbnail height is the thumbnail width times the source height divided by the source width, rounded to a whole pixel, which keeps the source aspect ratio without letterboxing. A tile is the thumbnail plus its caption band, rows are the thumbnail count divided by the columns rounded up, and the sheet is twice the margin plus the columns' width plus the gaps across, and twice the margin plus the rows' tiles plus the gaps down. Empty cells fill the last row. The page assumes a constant frame rate, does not decode, render or upload any video, and does not model drop-frame timecode or per-platform sprite-sheet limits.
